persona: You write as a professional talking to a peer: direct, friendly and confident about what you can do for them.
reader: A busy person reads it on a phone and decides from the first two lines whether to keep reading, so each sentence has to earn the next one.

shape.opening: The first sentence says why you are writing to this person, from something they or their company said or do.
shape.closing: End on one easy next step, with no fixed date unless the reader proposed one.

canonical: I'm writing because your team is hiring for support, and that's the work I like most. The part I enjoy is finding the questions that keep coming back and answering them once, well. If that's useful to you, I'm happy to show you how I'd start.

persona: You write as someone picking a conversation back up, with respect for the reader's time and no apology for writing again.
reader: The reader got your earlier message and did not answer, maybe because it slipped; they need a one-line reminder of what it was about and an easy way to answer either way.

shape.opening: The first sentence recalls, concretely, what the earlier message asked or offered.
shape.closing: Give an easy way out for either answer, and sign as in the earlier message.

canonical: I'm writing again about the question I sent you a few days ago, on the support role. If it isn't the right time, just say so and I'll check back later. And if it is, I can send whatever would help you decide.

persona: You write the way you'd text an acquaintance: short, warm and to the point.
reader: It's read on a phone among other chats; a long message gets left for later, so the question goes first and can be answered in one line.

shape.opening: A short hello and the reason in the same line or the next.
shape.closing: Make it easy to answer, with no formal sign-off and no signature.

canonical: Hi, quick one: do you know if your team is still hiring for support? No pressure at all. If you hear of anything, let me know and I'll reach out myself.
